label: chart.copy.contentDirection
why: AXChartDescriptor's own -copyWithZone: on the host leaves contentDirection at the zero case of its enumeration. Measured on the host: the original set to 5 by the case above, the copy answering 0, while every object-typed field of that same copy is carried - the title, the summary, the series array shared with the original, both axes and the additional axes. Measured again with six fields moved at once (a second host run, .agent-work/runs/accessibility/copyprobe.txt), and the only three the host's copies lose are contentDirection, contentFrame and AXNumericDataAxisDescriptor' scaleType: all three value-typed, every object-typed field carried. The port carries all three, because a copy that answers a zero rectangle and the linear case for values the caller set is a defect in the port, not the system behaving as documented. This row is that difference written out: the system column is what the host prints, the port column is what the port prints, and compare.py fails if either moves or if the two start agreeing.

label: chart.copy.contentFrame
why: As above, the same measured omission for the content frame. The frame is readwrite and the case sets it before it copies, so the port's copy answers what was set.

label: numeric.copy.scaleType
why: As above, the same measured omission for a numeric axis' scale type. No initialiser of that class takes a scale, so the port's -copyWithZone: sets the copy's own after the initialiser; the host's leaves it at the linear case. The bounds, the gridline positions, the title and the caller's own block are carried by both, and the case checks each of them on the copy.
